applied.problem: "The squaring is needed" is too absolute: averaging the plain sizes of the distances is another real measure of spread; squaring is one way to stop the signs cancelling. Also "every distance halves" holds only before the 0.01 ohm rounding.

Read alone, "if the mean and the median disagree, look for a stray reading" is too narrow: they also differ for a lopsided pile with no stray reading, and they rarely agree exactly, so it needs "by much" and the lopsided case.
